text: Muharrem İnce, a member of parliament for Yalova, was announced as the presidential candidate of the Republican People's Party (CHP) on 3 May 2018. The following day, on 4 May, party leader Kemal Kilicdaroglu formally declared the CHP's support for İnce. Shortly after, the CHP initiated campaign preparations, including the production of campaign materials and merchandise. In early May, it was revealed that İnce's campaign would use the slogan “Türkiye’ye güvence Muharrem İnce,” meaning "Muharrem İnce, an assurance to Turkey." The campaign launched with an election rally in Yalova on 5 May. In a 26 May interview on his campaign trail, İnce addressed the Turkish currency and debt crisis, stating that while the central bank could temporarily halt the lira’s slide by raising interest rates, depreciation does not fundamentally stem from interest rates being too high or too low; instead, political and legal reforms are essential to address economic uncertainty. He emphasized the need for independent and autonomous institutions to manage the economy and noted that his economic team had been working together for a long time. At campaign rallies, İnce pledged to allow education in the Kurdish language and to resolve the Kurdish issue through dialogue, not violence. On EU-Turkey relations, İnce supports Turkey’s bid to join the EU, which he traces back to the 1830s during the Ottoman Empire’s Tanzimat period, and highlights youth support for better employment opportunities as a key reason for deeper European integration. He also pledged to restore dignity to the Foreign Ministry’s professional diplomats, who are mocked by Islamist government trolls. Regarding Syria-Turkey relations, İnce proposed ending Turkey’s longstanding opposition to Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, arguing that cooperation would enable the return of the 3.5 million Syrian refugees living in Turkish camps. He stated during a rally that, “When I become president, we will have an ambassador to Syria.” Turkey severed diplomatic relations with Syria in 2012. As of 31 May, media reported that even die-hard CHP critics acknowledged İnce was performing far better than expected, due to his nationwide campaign focused on restoring democracy, the rule of law, better pay, and education. With respect to President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, İnce expressed a mix of contempt and near pity. Over the last week of May, İnce saw a 74 percent increase in social media popularity, reaching just over 1 million mentions and tags, close to Erdoğan’s 1.3 million, while competitors Meral Akşener had 280,852, Selahattin Demirtaş 201,922, and Temel Karamollaoğlu 181,703.
